Without it, an element present under more than one feature on the call is INVALID_INPUT (ambiguous) — e.g. template EFCALL 97 carries TOKENIZED_NM under GROUP_ASSOCIATION and EMPLOYER.

functions.notes: The BOM EXEC_ORDER is derived from the located row; only that row is removed. Check order: call selector, call existence, element_feature, element, BOM row.
functions.c_notes: C export deltas (SzConfigTool_deleteExpressionCallElement): addresses the call by EFCALL_ID only; element_feature NULL = None but "" is NOT coerced (NOT_FOUND); invalid UTF-8 in element_feature returns -1.

functions.name: add_standardize_call
functions.doc: Add a standardize call (CFG_SFCALL row) binding a standardize function to a feature or an element.

args.name: sfunc_code
args.semantics: Standardize function code (CFG_SFUNC, case-insensitive) or NOT_FOUND. Looked up before the feature/element.

args.name: ftype_code
args.semantics: Feature code (case-insensitive) or NOT_FOUND. "ALL" (case-insensitive) is treated as absent. Stored as FTYPE_ID; absent stores FTYPE_ID -1.

args.name: felem_code
args.semantics: Element code (case-insensitive) or NOT_FOUND. "N/A" (case-insensitive) is treated as absent. Stored as FELEM_ID; absent stores FELEM_ID -1. Exactly one of ftype_code / felem_code must resolve, else INVALID_INPUT.

args.name: exec_order
args.semantics: EXEC_ORDER scoped per (FTYPE_ID, FELEM_ID) of the new row (the -1 sentinel is part of the scope). Absent or <= 0 = auto-allocate (max in scope + 1, 1 for an empty scope); > 0 and free = used verbatim; > 0 and taken = ALREADY_EXISTS.

functions.notes: Returns (modified config, the new CFG_SFCALL row {SFCALL_ID, FTYPE_ID, FELEM_ID, SFUNC_ID, EXEC_ORDER}). SFCALL_ID is always auto-allocated (max + 1, floor 1000). MISSING_SECTION when CFG_SFCALL is absent. Check order: SFCALL_ID allocation, sfunc, feature, element, exactly-one rule, exec order. TRAP: the exec-order scope does not include SFUNC_ID, so a second call on the same feature continues that feature's order sequence.
functions.c_notes: C export deltas (SzConfigTool_addStandardizeCall): DROPS the new row; empty ftype_code / felem_code = None; negative exec_order = None; library errors return returnCode -5 with no reason code recorded (set_error, not set_error_from).

functions.name: delete_standardize_call
functions.doc: Delete a standardize call by SFCALL_ID.

args.name: sfcall_id
args.semantics: Must match an existing SFCALL_ID, else NOT_FOUND (also NOT_FOUND when CFG_SFCALL is absent).

functions.notes: Removes every CFG_SFCALL row with that id; no dependency checks (there is no standardize BOM).

functions.name: get_standardize_call
functions.doc: Get one standardize call's raw CFG_SFCALL row, by SFCALL_ID or by feature code.

args.name: call
args.semantics: Call selector: an integer = SFCALL_ID (NOT_FOUND if absent); a string = feature code (case-insensitive; unknown feature = NOT_FOUND, no call on the feature = NOT_FOUND, more than one call on the feature = INVALID_INPUT — address such calls by id). Any other JSON type = INVALID_INPUT.

functions.notes: Result uses on-disk keys (SFCALL_ID, FTYPE_ID, FELEM_ID, SFUNC_ID, EXEC_ORDER). Element-bound calls (FTYPE_ID -1) are never found by feature. In the template NAME has two standardize calls (PARSE_NAME, TOKENIZE_NAME), so by-feature NAME is ambiguous.
functions.c_notes: C export deltas: SzConfigTool_getStandardizeCall takes only an id and returns -5 (no reason code) on library errors; SzConfigTool_getStandardizeCallByFeature takes only a feature code and returns -2 with no reason code (set_error).

functions.name: list_standardize_calls
functions.doc: List all standardize calls with resolved codes.
functions.notes: Array of {id, feature, element, execOrder, function}, stably sorted by (FTYPE_ID, EXEC_ORDER). feature is "all" when FTYPE_ID <= 0 or unresolved; element is "n/a" when FELEM_ID <= 0 or unresolved; function is "unknown" when unresolved. No elementList key. Missing sections yield [] (no MISSING_SECTION).
functions.c_notes: C export returns -5 (no reason code) on library errors.

functions.name: add_standardize_call_element
functions.doc: Add a CFG_SFCALL row addressed by raw ids (FTYPE_ID, SFUNC_ID, FELEM_ID).

args.name: ftype_id
args.semantics: Stored verbatim as FTYPE_ID. NOT validated against CFG_FTYPE (use -1 for an element-bound row).

args.name: sfunc_id
args.semantics: Stored verbatim as SFUNC_ID. NOT validated against CFG_SFUNC.

args.name: felem_id
args.semantics: Stored as FELEM_ID; absent = -1. NOT validated against CFG_FELEM.

args.name: exec_order
args.semantics: EXEC_ORDER scoped per (FTYPE_ID, FELEM_ID). Absent or <= 0 = auto-allocate (max in scope + 1); > 0 and free = verbatim; > 0 and taken = ALREADY_EXISTS.

functions.notes: Returns (modified config, the new CFG_SFCALL row). ALREADY_PRESENT when a row with the same (FTYPE_ID, SFUNC_ID, FELEM_ID) exists (checked first). SFCALL_ID auto-allocated (max + 1, floor 1000); MISSING_SECTION when CFG_SFCALL is absent. Unlike add_standardize_call there is no feature-xor-element rule and no id validation.
functions.c_notes: No C export.

functions.name: delete_standardize_call_element
functions.doc: Delete CFG_SFCALL rows matching raw ids (FTYPE_ID, SFUNC_ID, FELEM_ID).

args.name: ftype_id
args.semantics: Matched against FTYPE_ID.

args.name: sfunc_id
args.semantics: Matched against SFUNC_ID.

args.name: felem_id
args.semantics: Matched against FELEM_ID; absent = -1.

functions.notes: NOT_FOUND (not NOT_ON_CALL) when no row matches. Removes EVERY matching row.
functions.c_notes: No C export.

functions.name: add_config_section
functions.doc: Add a new, empty top-level section (an empty array) to G2_CONFIG.

args.name: section_name
args.semantics: Uppercased before the duplicate check and storage. The new section is always an empty JSON array.

functions.notes: An existing key of the same (uppercased) name, of ANY JSON type, is ALREADY_EXISTS. A config without a G2_CONFIG key is NOT_FOUND (not MISSING_SECTION). No validation of the name (any string, e.g. not CFG_*, is accepted).

functions.name: remove_config_section
functions.doc: Remove a top-level section from G2_CONFIG.

args.name: section_name
args.semantics: Uppercased before lookup.

functions.notes: TRAP: no protection or dependency check; any section (including core sections such as CFG_DSRC, SETTINGS) can be removed. A missing section or a missing G2_CONFIG is NOT_FOUND.

functions.name: get_config_section
functions.doc: Get the raw items of a top-level section, optionally filtered by a case-insensitive substring.

args.name: section_name
args.semantics: TRAP: matched EXACTLY (case-sensitive, NOT uppercased, unlike add/remove_config_section). Unknown name is NOT_FOUND.

args.name: filter
args.semantics: Absent returns every item. Otherwise keeps items whose json.dumps-spaced rendering (`{"K": 1, "J": null}`, crate::filter::to_json_dumps_string) contains the filter, case-insensitively.

functions.notes: Result is an array. An array section returns its rows; a null or empty section returns []; a non-array, non-null section (e.g. SETTINGS, CONFIG_BASE_VERSION objects) returns a one-element array holding the value. An empty result does not distinguish "section empty" from "filter matched nothing": use config_section_is_empty.
functions.c_notes: C typed export reports a library error with returnCode -5 and NO reason code (set_error); a NULL filter pointer = absent.

functions.name: config_section_is_empty
functions.doc: Report whether a top-level section is empty (null or []).

args.name: section_name
args.semantics: Matched EXACTLY (case-sensitive, not uppercased). Unknown name is NOT_FOUND.

functions.notes: Result is a JSON boolean: true for null or [], false otherwise (any non-array, non-null value such as an object counts as non-empty).
functions.c_notes: C typed export returns the text "true"/"false"; library errors use returnCode -5 with no reason code.

functions.name: list_config_sections
functions.doc: List the names of all top-level G2_CONFIG keys.
functions.notes: Result is an array of key names in config order, including non-CFG keys (SETTINGS, SYS_OOM, CONFIG_BASE_VERSION). A missing or non-object G2_CONFIG yields [] rather than an error.
functions.c_notes: C typed export: library errors use returnCode -5 with no reason code.

functions.name: remove_config_section_field
functions.doc: Remove a field from every item of an array section, returning how many items had it.

args.name: section_name
args.semantics: Uppercased before lookup. Must name an ARRAY section, else NOT_FOUND.

args.name: field_name
args.semantics: Uppercased before removal (a lowercase key in a row can never be removed).

functions.notes: Record is the integer count of items the field was removed from (0 when no item had it; the config is still returned). Non-object items are skipped. A config with no G2_CONFIG key succeeds unchanged with count 0.
functions.c_notes: TRAP: the C typed export DROPS the count and reports library errors with returnCode -5 and no reason code; invoke keeps both halves.

functions.name: add_config_section_field
functions.doc: Add a field to every item of an array section that lacks it, returning existed/updated counts.

args.name: section_name
args.semantics: Uppercased before lookup. Must name an ARRAY section, else NOT_FOUND.

args.name: field_name
args.semantics: Uppercased before insertion.

args.name: field_value
args.semantics: Any JSON value, stored verbatim (cloned) into each item that lacks the field.

functions.notes: Record is {"existed": n, "updated": n}: items that already had the field (value preserved, never overwritten) vs. items it was inserted into. Non-object items are skipped (counted in neither). A config with no G2_CONFIG key succeeds unchanged with both counts 0.
functions.c_notes: C-EXPORT DELTA: SzConfigTool_addConfigSectionField takes the value as JSON text (invalid JSON = returnCode -3) and DROPS the counts; invoke keeps both halves.

functions.name: add_data_source
functions.doc: Add a data source (CFG_DSRC row) to the configuration.

args.name: code
args.semantics: Uppercased before storage and duplicate check; DSRC_DESC is set to the same uppercased code.

args.name: retention_level
args.semantics: Case-insensitive; normalized to Remember or Forget. Any other value is INVALID_INPUT.

args.name: id
args.semantics: Requested DSRC_ID. Absent OR <= 0 means auto-allocate (next free id, floor 1000). A taken id > 0 is ALREADY_EXISTS.

functions.c_notes: C typed export SzConfigTool_addDataSource exposes only `code` (retention_level and id always take their defaults); use SzConfigTool_invoke for the full surface.

functions.name: delete_data_source
functions.doc: Delete a data source by code.

args.name: code
args.semantics: Uppercased before lookup.

functions.notes: System data sources (DSRC_ID <= 2, e.g. TEST and SEARCH in the template) are protected and fail with INVALID_INPUT. No dependency check is made against other sections.

functions.name: get_data_source
functions.doc: Get one data source's raw CFG_DSRC row by code.

args.name: code
args.semantics: Uppercased before lookup.

functions.notes: Result is the stored row with on-disk keys (DSRC_ID, DSRC_CODE, DSRC_DESC, RETENTION_LEVEL).
functions.c_notes: LEGACY TRAP: the C typed export reports a library error with returnCode -5 and records NO reason code (it uses set_error, not set_error_from); SzConfigTool_invoke reports -2 with the reason code.

functions.name: list_data_sources
functions.doc: List all data sources as {id, dataSource} summaries.
functions.notes: Result is an array of {"id": DSRC_ID, "dataSource": DSRC_CODE} in config order.

functions.name: set_data_source
functions.doc: Update a data source's retention level.

args.name: code
args.semantics: Uppercased before lookup.

args.name: retention_level
args.semantics: Absent leaves RETENTION_LEVEL unchanged. TRAP: unlike add_data_source the value is written VERBATIM, with no domain validation or case normalization.

functions.c_notes: C typed export takes an updates JSON object whose key is camelCase `retentionLevel`; a non-string value there is silently ignored (treated as absent).

functions.name: add_element
functions.doc: Add an element (CFG_FELEM row).

args.name: code
args.semantics: Uppercased; duplicate (exact match on the uppercased code) is ALREADY_EXISTS.

args.name: description
args.semantics: FELEM_DESC, stored verbatim; absent defaults to the uppercased code.

args.name: data_type
args.semantics: Case-insensitive; normalized to lowercase string, number, date, datetime or json, else INVALID_INPUT.

args.name: id
args.semantics: Requested FELEM_ID. Absent OR <= 0 means auto-allocate (max existing + 1, floor 1000). A taken id > 0 is ALREADY_EXISTS.

functions.notes: Validation order: duplicate code, id, data_type.
functions.c_notes: C typed export SzConfigTool_addElement takes the code positionally plus an element JSON with keys description (or FELEM_DESC), dataType (or DATA_TYPE) and id; returns -3 (not -2) for invalid element JSON.

functions.name: delete_element
functions.doc: Delete an element that no feature uses.

args.name: code
args.semantics: Uppercased before lookup; unknown is NOT_FOUND.

functions.notes: INVALID_INPUT when any CFG_FBOM row maps the element to an existing feature ("Element linked to the following feature(s): ..."). TRAP: CFG_ATTR rows naming the element are NOT checked and are left dangling. MISSING_SECTION for an absent CFG_FELEM or CFG_FBOM; MISSING_FIELD when the matched row's FELEM_ID is not an integer.

functions.name: get_element
functions.doc: Get one element as a display summary by code.

args.name: code
args.semantics: Uppercased before lookup; unknown is NOT_FOUND.

functions.notes: Result is exactly {id, element, datatype}; FELEM_DESC is NOT included.

functions.name: list_elements
functions.doc: List all elements as display summaries, sorted by element code.
functions.notes: Array of {id, element, datatype}, sorted alphabetically by element code (not by id).

functions.name: set_element
functions.doc: Update an element's description and/or data type.

args.name: code
args.semantics: Uppercased before lookup; unknown is NOT_FOUND.

args.name: description
args.semantics: Absent leaves FELEM_DESC; else stored verbatim.

args.name: data_type
args.semantics: TRAP — absent leaves DATA_TYPE; else stored VERBATIM with no validation or normalization (unlike add_element).

functions.notes: Succeeds unchanged when no update args are given.
functions.c_notes: C typed export takes an updates JSON with keys description (or FELEM_DESC) and dataType (or DATA_TYPE); returns -3 for invalid updates JSON.

functions.name: set_feature_element
functions.doc: Update one feature-element (CFG_FBOM) row's exec order, display level, delimiter or derived flag.

args.name: feature_code
args.semantics: Required. Case-insensitive; unknown is NOT_FOUND.

args.name: element_code
args.semantics: Required. Case-insensitive; unknown is NOT_FOUND.

args.name: exec_order
args.semantics: TRAP — stored verbatim; no uniqueness check and no <= 0 auto-allocation.

args.name: display_level
args.semantics: Must be >= 0, else INVALID_INPUT.

args.name: display_delim
args.semantics: Stored verbatim. Not tri-state; cannot be cleared back to null.

args.name: derived
args.semantics: Case-insensitive Yes/No, normalized, else INVALID_INPUT.

functions.notes: NOT_FOUND when the (feature, element) mapping is absent. Succeeds unchanged when no update args are given. A missing CFG_FTYPE/CFG_FELEM surfaces as NOT_FOUND (code lookup).
functions.c_notes: No C typed export.

functions.name: add_element_to_feature
functions.doc: Map an existing element to a feature (append a CFG_FBOM row).

args.name: feature_code
args.semantics: Case-insensitive; unknown is NOT_FOUND.

args.name: element_code
args.semantics: Case-insensitive; unknown is NOT_FOUND (the element is never auto-created).

args.name: display_level
args.semantics: Must be >= 0, else INVALID_INPUT.

args.name: display_delim
args.semantics: Stored verbatim; absent stores null.

args.name: derived
args.semantics: Case-insensitive Yes/No, normalized, else INVALID_INPUT.

functions.notes: EXEC_ORDER is always auto-allocated as max(EXEC_ORDER over the WHOLE CFG_FBOM table) + 1 and cannot be requested (use features.add_feature_comparison for an explicit order). Duplicate (FTYPE_ID, FELEM_ID) is ALREADY_EXISTS. Validation order: feature, element, display_level, derived, CFG_FBOM section, duplicate.
functions.c_notes: C typed export takes an optional options JSON (null allowed) with keys displayLevel, displayDelim, derived; mistyped values are silently ignored; returns -3 for invalid options JSON.

functions.name: delete_element_from_feature
functions.doc: Remove one feature-element (CFG_FBOM) mapping.

args.name: feature_code
args.semantics: Case-insensitive; unknown is NOT_FOUND.

args.name: element_code
args.semantics: Case-insensitive; unknown is NOT_FOUND.

functions.notes: NOT_FOUND when the mapping is absent. The CFG_FELEM row is kept.

functions.name: render_config
functions.doc: Render a config document in canonical export form (recursively key-sorted, pretty-printed).

args.name: indent
args.semantics: Spaces per indentation level, applied verbatim (2 = CLI on-disk form, 4 = Python parity; 0 allowed). Negative is INVALID_INPUT (raised by the req_usize converter, before the library is called).

functions.notes: Result is a JSON STRING holding the rendered text (not the working config envelope): every object's keys sorted recursively (Python json.dumps(sort_keys=True)), array order kept, no trailing newline. The text is itself a valid config and may be passed back in. Any JSON document is accepted (no G2_CONFIG check).
functions.c_notes: C typed export deltas: a negative indent is coerced to 0 instead of rejected, and the rendered text is returned as the bare response.

functions.name: add_feature
functions.doc: Add a feature (CFG_FTYPE row) with its element list (CFG_FBOM rows) and optional standardize/expression/comparison calls.

args.name: feature
args.semantics: Uppercased; stored as FTYPE_CODE and FTYPE_DESC. Duplicate (exact match on the uppercased code) is ALREADY_EXISTS.

args.name: element_list
args.semantics: Must be a non-empty JSON array, else INVALID_INPUT. Each item is either an element-code string, or an object with `element` (or `ELEMENT`, required, else INVALID_INPUT) and optional `expressed`/`EXPRESSED`, `compared`/`COMPARED` ("yes" case-insensitive = true), `display`/`DISPLAY` ("yes" = DISPLAY_LEVEL 1, anything else 0) or `displaylevel`/`DISPLAYLEVEL`/`display_level` (int, default 1, negative = INVALID_INPUT), `displaydelim`/`DISPLAYDELIM`/`display_delim`, `derived`/`DERIVED` (Yes/No case-insensitive, else INVALID_INPUT; default No). Any other item type is INVALID_INPUT. Element codes are uppercased; a code not in CFG_FELEM is AUTO-CREATED (FELEM_ID max+1 floor 1000, DATA_TYPE string, FELEM_DESC = code). The FBOM EXEC_ORDER is the item's 1-based position (per feature, not whole-table).

args.name: class
args.semantics: CFG_FCLASS code, case-insensitive; unknown is NOT_FOUND.

args.name: behavior
args.semantics: Behavior code (A1, F1, FF, FM, FVM, NONE, NAME; E/S suffixes set FTYPE_EXCL/FTYPE_STAB), case-insensitive; otherwise INVALID_INPUT.

args.name: candidates
args.semantics: USED_FOR_CAND; case-insensitive Yes/No, normalized, else INVALID_INPUT.

args.name: anonymize
args.semantics: ANONYMIZE; case-insensitive Yes/No, normalized, else INVALID_INPUT.

args.name: derived
args.semantics: DERIVED; case-insensitive Yes/No, normalized, else INVALID_INPUT.

args.name: history
args.semantics: PERSIST_HISTORY; case-insensitive Yes/No, normalized, else INVALID_INPUT.

args.name: matchkey
args.semantics: SHOW_IN_MATCH_KEY; case-insensitive Yes, No, Confirm or Denial, normalized, else INVALID_INPUT. Absent defaults to Yes when `comparison` is given, else No.

args.name: standardize
args.semantics: CFG_SFUNC code (case-insensitive) or NOT_FOUND (an empty string is looked up too, so "" is NOT_FOUND). Creates a CFG_SFCALL row (SFCALL_ID max+1 floor 1000, EXEC_ORDER 1, FELEM_ID -1).

args.name: expression
args.semantics: CFG_EFUNC code (case-insensitive) or NOT_FOUND ("" is NOT_FOUND). Requires at least one element_list item with expressed=yes, else INVALID_INPUT. Creates a CFG_EFCALL row (EFCALL_ID max+1 floor 1000, EXEC_ORDER 1) and a CFG_EFBOM row (FELEM_REQ Yes) per expressed element.

args.name: comparison
args.semantics: CFG_CFUNC code (case-insensitive) or NOT_FOUND ("" is NOT_FOUND). Requires at least one element_list item with compared=yes, else INVALID_INPUT. Creates a CFG_CFCALL row (CFCALL_ID max+1 floor 1000) and a CFG_CFBOM row per compared element.

args.name: version
args.semantics: Stored verbatim in VERSION.

args.name: rtype_id
args.semantics: Stored verbatim in RTYPE_ID; not validated against CFG_RTYPE.

args.name: id
args.semantics: Requested FTYPE_ID. Absent OR <= 0 means auto-allocate (max existing + 1, floor 1000). A taken id > 0 is ALREADY_EXISTS.

functions.notes: Validation order: CFG_FTYPE section, duplicate code, element_list shape, candidates/anonymize/derived/history/matchkey domains, id, behavior, class, function codes, expressed/compared counts, then per-element (display level, derived). The input config is never modified on error.
functions.c_notes: C typed export SzConfigTool_addFeature takes the code positionally plus a feature JSON with keys elementList (or element_list), class, behavior, candidates, anonymize, derived, history, matchkey (or matchKey), standardize, expression, comparison, version, rtype_id (or rtypeId), id; non-string/non-int values are silently ignored. NON-STANDARD return codes: -3 for invalid feature JSON or a missing elementList, -4 C-string failure, -5 for EVERY library error (not -2).

functions.name: delete_feature
functions.doc: Delete a feature and cascade-delete its FBOM rows, attributes and standardize/expression/comparison/distinct calls.

args.name: feature
args.semantics: A string that parses (after trim) as an integer is an FTYPE_ID; otherwise a feature code, uppercased. Unknown is NOT_FOUND.

functions.notes: Locked features NAME, ADDRESS, PHONE, DOB, REL_LINK, REL_ANCHOR, REL_POINTER are INVALID_INPUT. Cascade removes the feature's CFG_FBOM rows, CFG_ATTR rows whose FTYPE_CODE matches, CFG_SFCALL, CFG_EFCALL (+ their CFG_EFBOM), CFG_CFCALL (+ CFG_CFBOM) and CFG_DFCALL (+ CFG_DFBOM) rows; CFG_FELEM rows are kept. A missing CFG_FTYPE is MISSING_SECTION for an id but NOT_FOUND for a code.

functions.name: get_feature
functions.doc: Get one feature as a display summary including its elementList.

args.name: feature
args.semantics: Integer string (after trim) = FTYPE_ID; otherwise a code, uppercased.

functions.notes: Result {id, feature, class, behavior, anonymize, candidates, standardize, expression, comparison, matchKey, version, elementList}; elementList items {element, expressed, compared, derived, display} sorted by EXEC_ORDER, display = "No" iff DISPLAY_LEVEL is 0. standardize/expression/comparison are "" when absent. DERIVED, PERSIST_HISTORY and RTYPE_ID of the feature are NOT in the result. A missing CFG_FTYPE section is NOT_FOUND (never MISSING_SECTION).

functions.name: list_features
functions.doc: List all features as display summaries, sorted by FTYPE_ID.
functions.notes: Array of the same objects get_feature returns.

functions.name: set_feature
functions.doc: Update a feature's flags, behavior, class, version or RTYPE_ID.

args.name: feature
args.semantics: Integer string (after trim) = FTYPE_ID; otherwise a code, uppercased. Unknown is NOT_FOUND.

args.name: candidates
args.semantics: USED_FOR_CAND; case-insensitive Yes/No, normalized, else INVALID_INPUT.

args.name: anonymize
args.semantics: TRAP — stored VERBATIM in ANONYMIZE (no validation or normalization, unlike add_feature).

args.name: derived
args.semantics: TRAP — stored VERBATIM in DERIVED (no validation or normalization).

args.name: history
args.semantics: TRAP — stored VERBATIM in PERSIST_HISTORY (no validation or normalization).

args.name: matchkey
args.semantics: SHOW_IN_MATCH_KEY; case-insensitive Yes, No, Confirm or Denial, normalized, else INVALID_INPUT.

args.name: behavior
args.semantics: Behavior code (case-insensitive) parsed into FTYPE_FREQ/FTYPE_EXCL/FTYPE_STAB, else INVALID_INPUT.

args.name: class
args.semantics: CFG_FCLASS code, case-insensitive; unknown is NOT_FOUND.

args.name: version
args.semantics: Stored verbatim in VERSION.

args.name: rtype_id
args.semantics: Stored verbatim in RTYPE_ID; not validated.

functions.notes: If no supplied value differs from the stored row (including when no update args are given) the call fails with INVALID_INPUT "No changes detected". The input config is never modified on error.
functions.c_notes: C typed export takes an updates JSON with keys candidates, anonymize, derived, history, matchkey (or matchKey), behavior, class, version, rtypeId (or RTYPE_ID); mistyped values are silently ignored.

functions.name: add_feature_comparison
functions.doc: Add a feature-element (CFG_FBOM) row with an optional explicit EXEC_ORDER.

args.name: feature_code
args.semantics: Required. Feature code, case-insensitive; unknown is NOT_FOUND.

args.name: element_code
args.semantics: Required. Element code, case-insensitive; unknown is NOT_FOUND.

args.name: exec_order
args.semantics: WHOLE-TABLE scope: absent or <= 0 auto-allocates max(EXEC_ORDER over all of CFG_FBOM) + 1; a value > 0 already used by ANY CFG_FBOM row is ALREADY_EXISTS.

args.name: display_level
args.semantics: TRAP — stored verbatim, NOT validated, and absent stores DISPLAY_LEVEL null (no default 1, unlike add_element_to_feature).

args.name: display_delim
args.semantics: Stored verbatim; absent stores null.

args.name: derived
args.semantics: TRAP — stored verbatim, NOT validated; absent stores DERIVED null.

functions.notes: Writes the same table as elements.add_element_to_feature. Duplicate (FTYPE_ID, FELEM_ID) is ALREADY_EXISTS. A missing CFG_FTYPE/CFG_FELEM section surfaces as NOT_FOUND (code lookup); a missing CFG_FBOM as MISSING_SECTION.
functions.c_notes: No C typed export.

functions.name: delete_feature_comparison
functions.doc: Delete one feature-element (CFG_FBOM) row.

args.name: feature_code
args.semantics: Case-insensitive; unknown is NOT_FOUND.

functions.notes: Returns (config, {plan_id, was_created}). Existing code: only GPLAN_DESC is replaced (other keys kept), was_created false. New code: a row with GPLAN_ID = max + 1 is appended, was_created true; an absent CFG_GPLAN section is MISSING_SECTION on this create path.
functions.c_notes: C-EXPORT DELTA: SzConfigTool_setGenericPlan DROPS plan_id and was_created and reports library errors with returnCode -5 and no reason code.

functions.name: add_rule
functions.doc: Add an entity resolution rule (CFG_ERRULE row), returning the assigned ERRULE_ID.

args.name: id
args.semantics: Requested ERRULE_ID. 0 or any negative value means auto-allocate (max existing + 1, floor 1000, so 1000 on the template). A taken id > 0 is ALREADY_EXISTS. Any ERRULE_ID key inside rule_config is IGNORED.

args.name: rule_config
args.semantics: Object with on-disk keys. ERRULE_CODE (string) is required, else MISSING_FIELD; uppercased for storage and the case-insensitive duplicate check (ALREADY_EXISTS). QUAL_ERFRAG_CODE (the fragment) is required: absent/non-string is MISSING_FIELD, "" or an unknown code is NOT_FOUND (existence is case-insensitive). DISQ_ERFRAG_CODE is optional: "" is accepted and stored as "", an unknown code is NOT_FOUND. TRAP: both fragment codes are stored VERBATIM (not uppercased). RESOLVE / RELATE default "No", must be Yes/No case-insensitively (stored title-case) else INVALID_INPUT, and may not both be Yes (INVALID_INPUT). RESOLVE=Yes requires a non-zero ERRULE_TIER (INVALID_INPUT) and forces RTYPE_ID to 1; RELATE=Yes requires RTYPE_ID in 2,3,4 (INVALID_INPUT). RTYPE_ID defaults to 1; ERRULE_TIER defaults to null. A non-string / non-integer value for any of these keys is treated as absent.

functions.notes: Record is the assigned ERRULE_ID (integer). The written row always carries every CFG_ERRULE key (ERRULE_ID, ERRULE_CODE, RESOLVE, RELATE, RTYPE_ID, QUAL_ERFRAG_CODE, DISQ_ERFRAG_CODE, ERRULE_TIER; optional ones as null). ERRULE_CODE is checked BEFORE the config is parsed, so a missing code is MISSING_FIELD even for invalid config JSON. A config without CFG_ERRULE is MISSING_SECTION (after validation). Validation order: fragment, disqualifier, duplicate code, RESOLVE, RELATE, exclusivity, tier, RTYPE_ID.
functions.c_notes: C typed export deltas: SzConfigTool_addRule takes one rule JSON and reads the id from its ERRULE_ID key (absent/non-integer = 0 = auto-allocate), DROPS the assigned id, and reports library errors with returnCode -5 and no reason code.

functions.name: delete_rule
functions.doc: Delete a rule by code.

args.name: code
args.semantics: Uppercased, then matched EXACTLY against ERRULE_CODE (a stored lowercase code cannot be deleted). Not an id.

functions.notes: No dependency or system-rule protection; any rule can be deleted. A config without CFG_ERRULE is NOT_FOUND.

functions.name: get_rule
functions.doc: Get one rule, by code or ERRULE_ID, as a summary record.

args.name: code_or_id
args.semantics: Uppercased, then matched exactly against ERRULE_CODE first, then numerically against ERRULE_ID (e.g. "100").

functions.notes: Result is {id, rule, resolve, relate, rtype_id, fragment, disqualifier, tier} projected from ERRULE_ID, ERRULE_CODE, RESOLVE, RELATE, RTYPE_ID, QUAL_ERFRAG_CODE, DISQ_ERFRAG_CODE (null-preserving). TRAP: `tier` is the stored ERRULE_TIER only when RESOLVE is exactly "Yes", otherwise null.
functions.c_notes: C typed export reports library errors with returnCode -5 and no reason code.

functions.name: list_rules
functions.doc: List all rules as summary records, sorted by ERRULE_ID.
functions.notes: Result is an array of the get_rule record shape, sorted by id ascending (null/absent id sorts as 0). A missing CFG_ERRULE or G2_CONFIG yields [].
functions.c_notes: C typed export reports library errors with returnCode -5 and no reason code.

functions.name: set_rule
functions.doc: Update a rule's resolve/relate/relationship type, fragment, disqualifier or tier.

args.name: code
args.semantics: Rule code; uppercased, then matched exactly. Unknown is NOT_FOUND.

args.name: resolve
args.semantics: Absent keeps the stored RESOLVE. Must be Yes/No case-insensitively (stored title-case), else INVALID_INPUT.

args.name: relate
args.semantics: Absent keeps the stored RELATE. Must be Yes/No case-insensitively, else INVALID_INPUT.

args.name: rtype_id
args.semantics: Absent keeps the stored RTYPE_ID. Forced to 1 when the merged RESOLVE is Yes; must be 2, 3 or 4 when RELATE is Yes.

args.name: fragment
args.semantics: QUAL_ERFRAG_CODE. Absent = keep (never re-validated); null = clear to null (TRAP: allowed here although add_rule requires a fragment); a string must name an existing fragment (case-insensitive; "" is NOT_FOUND) and is stored UPPERCASED (unlike add_rule).

args.name: disqualifier
args.semantics: DISQ_ERFRAG_CODE. Absent = keep; null = clear to null; "" is accepted and stored ""; another string must name an existing fragment (NOT_FOUND) and is stored uppercased.

args.name: tier
args.semantics: ERRULE_TIER. Absent = keep; null = clear; value = set. The merged rule with RESOLVE=Yes must have a non-zero tier, else INVALID_INPUT.

functions.notes: Merges the update into the stored row and re-applies add_rule's RESOLVE/RELATE/exclusivity/tier/RTYPE_ID rules to the merged row (no duplicate-code check); the row is rewritten with every CFG_ERRULE key and ERRULE_ID preserved.
functions.c_notes: C typed export SzConfigTool_setRule takes the code plus an update JSON whose keys are resolve|RESOLVE, relate|RELATE, rtypeId|RTYPE_ID (camelCase), fragment|FRAGMENT, disqualifier|DISQUALIFIER, tier|TIER; there a null value = clear and a value of the wrong JSON type is silently treated as absent.

functions.name: add_search_profile
functions.doc: Add a search profile (CFG_SPROFILE row) tying a generic plan and feature candidate overrides to a code.

args.name: code
args.semantics: SPROFILE_CODE; trimmed and uppercased. Empty after trimming is INVALID_INPUT; an existing code (case-insensitive) is ALREADY_EXISTS.

args.name: generic_plan
args.semantics: GPLAN_CODE, matched case-insensitively against CFG_GPLAN (NOT_FOUND); stored as GPLAN_ID.

args.name: candidates
args.semantics: DEFAULT_USED_FOR_CAND; trimmed, case-insensitive, normalized to Normal or Off. Absent or blank = Normal. Anything else is VALIDATION_ERRORS (field "candidates", OUT_OF_DOMAIN).

args.name: description
args.semantics: SPROFILE_DESC, stored verbatim; absent = "".

args.name: elements
args.semantics: Feature candidate overrides: an array of {"feature": FTYPE_CODE, "flag": Yes|No|Y|N} objects (only those two keys, both strings, else INVALID_INPUT; a missing key = MISSING_FIELD); absent = none. Each feature is resolved case-insensitively against CFG_FTYPE (NOT_FOUND); a feature listed twice is VALIDATION_ERRORS (field "overrides", DUPLICATE); a flag other than Yes/Y/No/N (trimmed, case-insensitive) is VALIDATION_ERRORS (field "overrides", OUT_OF_DOMAIN). Stored in FTYPE_OVERRIDES as "[{<ftypeId>,<Y|N>},...]" sorted by FTYPE_ID, or "[]".

functions.notes: SPROFILE_ID is always auto-allocated (max + 1, floor 1; 3 on the template, whose only profile is SEARCH = 2); no explicit id can be requested. CFG_SPROFILE is created when absent. Validation order: code, candidates, generic plan, overrides (per element: feature, duplicate, flag), duplicate code. A config without G2_CONFIG fails the generic-plan lookup (NOT_FOUND), so the library's MISSING_SECTION branch is unreachable; a non-array CFG_SPROFILE is INVALID_STRUCTURE.
functions.c_notes: No typed C export; use SzConfigTool_invoke.

functions.name: get_search_profile
functions.doc: Get one search profile's raw CFG_SPROFILE row by code.

args.name: code
args.semantics: Case-insensitive match against SPROFILE_CODE. Not an id.

functions.notes: Result is the stored row (SPROFILE_ID, SPROFILE_CODE, SPROFILE_DESC, GPLAN_ID, DEFAULT_USED_FOR_CAND, FTYPE_OVERRIDES). A missing section is NOT_FOUND.
functions.c_notes: No typed C export; use SzConfigTool_invoke.

functions.name: list_search_profiles
functions.doc: List search profiles as display records with ids resolved to codes, sorted by id.

args.name: filter
args.semantics: Absent returns all. Otherwise keeps rows whose COMPACT raw-row JSON (serde_json::to_string, no spaces, on-disk keys and ids, e.g. "GPLAN_ID":2) contains the filter case-insensitively; it is applied to the raw row, not the projected record.

functions.notes: Result is an array of {id, profile, description, genericPlan, candidates, overrides: [{feature, flag: Yes|No}], overridesRaw} sorted by id. genericPlan / feature fall back to the numeric id as a string when unresolvable. A missing CFG_SPROFILE yields [].
functions.c_notes: No typed C export; use SzConfigTool_invoke.

functions.name: delete_search_profile
functions.doc: Delete a search profile by code or SPROFILE_ID.

args.name: search_value
args.semantics: Matched case-insensitively against SPROFILE_CODE, or (when it parses as an integer after trimming) against SPROFILE_ID.

functions.notes: The shipped profiles INGEST and SEARCH are protected: deleting one that exists is INVALID_INPUT. Existence is checked FIRST, so an absent reserved code (INGEST is not in the template) is NOT_FOUND.
functions.c_notes: No typed C export; use SzConfigTool_invoke.

functions.name: set_setting
functions.doc: Create or overwrite a named setting in the G2_CONFIG.SETTINGS object.

args.name: name
args.semantics: Uppercased; an existing setting of that name is overwritten silently.

args.name: value
args.semantics: Stored VERBATIM as its typed JSON value (an integer stays an integer, a string a string); no validation.

functions.notes: SETTINGS is created when absent, and a non-object SETTINGS value (null, string, array) is REPLACED by a fresh object (prior content lost). A missing or non-object G2_CONFIG is MISSING_SECTION.
functions.c_notes: C typed export takes the value as JSON text; text that is not valid JSON is INVALID_INPUT there.

functions.name: list_system_parameters
functions.doc: List system parameters as a name -> string-value map.
functions.notes: Result is an object. The only parameter is relationshipsBreakMatches, read from BREAK_RES of the FIRST CFG_RTYPE row with RCLASS_ID 2 and reported as a decimal STRING. TRAP: it is reported only when BREAK_RES is a JSON integer; the template's DISCLOSED row stores the string "No", so the template yields {}. A missing CFG_RTYPE/G2_CONFIG also yields {}.
functions.c_notes: C typed export reports library errors with returnCode -5 and no reason code.

functions.name: set_system_parameter
functions.doc: Set a system parameter (relationshipsBreakMatches).

args.name: parameter_name
args.semantics: Case-insensitive; only relationshipsBreakMatches (or relationships_break_matches) is known. Any other name is INVALID_CONFIG (not INVALID_INPUT).

args.name: parameter_value
args.semantics: Written VERBATIM (any JSON value, no validation) to BREAK_RES of the first CFG_RTYPE row with RCLASS_ID 2. Only an integer value is visible to list_system_parameters afterwards.

functions.notes: NOT_FOUND when no CFG_RTYPE row has RCLASS_ID 2 (or CFG_RTYPE/G2_CONFIG is absent). The parameter name is checked AFTER the config is parsed.
functions.c_notes: C export SzConfigTool_setSystemParameterWithJson (the only C entry point) takes the value as JSON text.

functions.name: add_comparison_threshold
functions.doc: Add a comparison threshold (CFG_CFRTN row) for a comparison function, feature and return value.

args.name: cfunc_code
args.semantics: REQUIRED by the library (absent = MISSING_FIELD). Comparison function code (CFG_CFUNC), matched case-insensitively; unknown = NOT_FOUND.

args.name: ftype_code
args.semantics: REQUIRED by the library (absent = MISSING_FIELD). Feature code matched case-insensitively (unknown = NOT_FOUND), or "all" (any case) for the all-features FTYPE_ID 0 sentinel.

args.name: cfunc_rtnval
args.semantics: REQUIRED by the library (absent = MISSING_FIELD). Return value / score name; uppercased before storage and duplicate check.

args.name: exec_order
args.semantics: Resolved in three steps: (1) if an all-features (FTYPE_ID 0) row already exists for this (cfunc, rtnval), its EXEC_ORDER is REUSED and this arg is ignored; (2) else a value > 0 is honoured, or ALREADY_EXISTS if taken within (CFUNC_ID, FTYPE_ID 0); (3) else (absent or <= 0) the next order within (CFUNC_ID, FTYPE_ID 0) is auto-allocated (max + 1). Never null.

args.name: same_score
args.semantics: Stored verbatim (no range check); absent stores SAME_SCORE null.

args.name: close_score
args.semantics: Stored verbatim; absent stores CLOSE_SCORE null.

args.name: likely_score
args.semantics: Stored verbatim; absent stores LIKELY_SCORE null.

args.name: plausible_score
args.semantics: Stored verbatim; absent stores PLAUSIBLE_SCORE null.

args.name: un_likely_score
args.semantics: Stored verbatim; absent stores UN_LIKELY_SCORE null.

functions.notes: CFRTN_ID is always auto-allocated (max existing + 1, no floor); there is no id arg. Duplicate key is (CFUNC_ID, FTYPE_ID, uppercased rtnval) = ALREADY_EXISTS. Order: missing fields, cfunc lookup, feature lookup, then CFG_CFRTN section, duplicate, exec order.
functions.c_notes: C-EXPORT DELTA: SzConfigTool_addComparisonThreshold is ID-based (calls the doc-hidden add_comparison_threshold_by_id): takes CFUNC_ID / FTYPE_ID integers, never validates they exist, and maps a NEGATIVE value of ftype_id (-> 0 = all), exec_order and every score to None, so a negative score cannot be stored through C; invoke takes codes and stores any integer.

functions.name: delete_comparison_threshold
functions.doc: Delete a comparison threshold identified by (comparison function, feature, return value).

args.name: cfunc_code
args.semantics: Comparison function code, case-insensitive; unknown = NOT_FOUND.

args.name: ftype_code
args.semantics: Feature code (case-insensitive) or "all" for FTYPE_ID 0; unknown = NOT_FOUND.

args.name: cfunc_rtnval
args.semantics: Return value, matched case-insensitively.

functions.notes: No matching row = NOT_FOUND. No tier/dependency protection: deleting the all-features tier row leaves per-feature rows in place.
functions.c_notes: C-EXPORT DELTA: SzConfigTool_deleteComparisonThreshold takes a CFRTN_ID instead (doc-hidden delete_comparison_threshold_by_id); a missing CFG_CFRTN section there is NOT_FOUND, not MISSING_SECTION.

functions.name: set_comparison_threshold
functions.doc: Update the exec order and/or scores of an existing comparison threshold.

args.name: cfunc_code
args.semantics: REQUIRED by the library (absent = MISSING_FIELD). Case-insensitive lookup; unknown = NOT_FOUND.

args.name: ftype_code
args.semantics: REQUIRED (absent = MISSING_FIELD). Feature code (case-insensitive) or "all" for FTYPE_ID 0.

args.name: cfunc_rtnval
args.semantics: REQUIRED (absent = MISSING_FIELD). Matched case-insensitively; no row = NOT_FOUND.

args.name: exec_order
args.semantics: Absent leaves EXEC_ORDER unchanged; a value is written VERBATIM (no uniqueness / tier check, any integer incl. <= 0).

args.name: same_score
args.semantics: Absent leaves unchanged; else written verbatim.

args.name: close_score
args.semantics: Absent leaves unchanged; else written verbatim.

args.name: likely_score
args.semantics: Absent leaves unchanged; else written verbatim.

args.name: plausible_score
args.semantics: Absent leaves unchanged; else written verbatim.

args.name: un_likely_score
args.semantics: Absent leaves unchanged; else written verbatim.

functions.notes: NOT tri-state: a score cannot be cleared back to null.
functions.c_notes: C-EXPORT DELTA: SzConfigTool_setComparisonThreshold is keyed by CFRTN_ID (doc-hidden set_comparison_threshold_by_id) and takes an updates JSON object with camelCase keys sameScore, closeScore, likelyScore, plausibleScore, unlikelyScore; it CANNOT change EXEC_ORDER, and a non-integer value there is silently ignored. Invalid updates JSON returns returnCode -3 (boundary error, no reason code).

functions.name: list_comparison_thresholds
functions.doc: List all comparison thresholds with resolved function and feature names.
functions.notes: Array of {id (CFRTN_ID), function (CFUNC_CODE or "unknown"), returnOrder (EXEC_ORDER), scoreName, feature ("all" for FTYPE_ID 0, else FTYPE_CODE or "unknown"), sameScore, closeScore, likelyScore, plausibleScore, unlikelyScore}, sorted by (CFUNC_ID, CFRTN_ID). TRAP: null/absent EXEC_ORDER and scores are reported as 0, not null. Requires CFG_CFRTN, CFG_CFUNC and CFG_FTYPE (else MISSING_SECTION).

functions.name: add_generic_threshold
functions.doc: Add a generic threshold (CFG_GENERIC_THRESHOLD row) for a plan, behavior and optional feature.

args.name: plan
args.semantics: REQUIRED (absent = MISSING_FIELD). Uppercased, then matched EXACTLY against GPLAN_CODE (so effectively case-insensitive for upper-case stored codes); unknown = NOT_FOUND.

args.name: behavior
args.semantics: REQUIRED (absent = MISSING_FIELD). Uppercased; must be a canonical behavior code (behavior_domain, e.g. NAME, F1, FM, A1) else VALIDATION_ERRORS (field "behavior", UnknownReferenceCode).

args.name: scoring_cap
args.semantics: REQUIRED (absent = MISSING_FIELD). Stored verbatim (e.g. -1).

args.name: candidate_cap
args.semantics: REQUIRED (absent = MISSING_FIELD). Stored verbatim.

args.name: send_to_redo
args.semantics: REQUIRED (absent = MISSING_FIELD). Case-insensitive Yes/No, stored canonical "Yes"/"No"; else VALIDATION_ERRORS (field "sendToRedo", OutOfDomain).

args.name: feature
args.semantics: Absent or "all" (any case) = FTYPE_ID 0. Else uppercased and matched EXACTLY against FTYPE_CODE; unknown = NOT_FOUND.

functions.notes: All absent required fields are reported in ONE MISSING_FIELD (order plan, behavior, scoring_cap, candidate_cap, send_to_redo), checked before the config is parsed. Then: plan lookup, feature lookup, duplicate (plan, behavior, feature) = ALREADY_EXISTS (Python treats it as a warning-success; the root library does not), then behavior + sendToRedo are validated TOGETHER into one VALIDATION_ERRORS (details schema sz-configtool.validation-errors/v1, order [behavior, sendToRedo]).
functions.c_notes: C typed export SzConfigTool_addGenericThreshold takes every arg (feature NULL = ALL) with no coercions.

functions.name: delete_generic_threshold
functions.doc: Delete a generic threshold identified by (plan, behavior, feature).

args.name: plan
args.semantics: REQUIRED (absent = MISSING_FIELD). Case-insensitive GPLAN_CODE lookup; unknown = NOT_FOUND.

args.name: behavior
args.semantics: REQUIRED (absent = MISSING_FIELD). Uppercased and matched exactly; NOT validated against the behavior domain (no row = NOT_FOUND).

args.name: feature
args.semantics: Absent or "all" = FTYPE_ID 0; else uppercased exact FTYPE_CODE match, unknown = NOT_FOUND.

functions.notes: No matching row = NOT_FOUND (also when CFG_GENERIC_THRESHOLD is absent). (Before the Unreleased fix it ignored `plan` and always deleted from INGEST.)
functions.c_notes: C typed export SzConfigTool_deleteGenericThreshold takes every arg (feature NULL = ALL) with no coercions.

functions.name: set_generic_threshold
functions.doc: Update the caps and/or send-to-redo flag of an existing generic threshold.

args.name: plan
args.semantics: REQUIRED (absent = MISSING_FIELD). Case-insensitive GPLAN_CODE lookup; unknown = NOT_FOUND.

args.name: behavior
args.semantics: REQUIRED (absent = MISSING_FIELD). Lookup KEY only: uppercased and matched exactly, never validated against the domain (no row = NOT_FOUND).

args.name: feature
args.semantics: Lookup KEY selecting the per-feature row (never written). Absent or "all" = FTYPE_ID 0; else case-insensitive feature lookup, unknown = NOT_FOUND.

args.name: candidate_cap
args.semantics: Absent leaves CANDIDATE_CAP unchanged; else written verbatim.

args.name: scoring_cap
args.semantics: Absent leaves SCORING_CAP unchanged; else written verbatim.

args.name: send_to_redo
args.semantics: Absent leaves unchanged; else case-insensitive Yes/No stored canonical, otherwise VALIDATION_ERRORS (field "sendToRedo", OutOfDomain) — checked AFTER the row lookup, so a missing row wins.

functions.c_notes: C-EXPORT DELTA: SzConfigTool_setGenericThreshold takes a GPLAN_ID integer (unknown id = returnCode -4 with no reason code) plus behavior, and an updates JSON with camelCase keys candidateCap, scoringCap, sendToRedo, feature; a non-integer cap there is INVALID_INPUT, a non-string sendToRedo/feature is silently ignored; invalid updates JSON = returnCode -3.

functions.name: list_generic_thresholds
functions.doc: List all generic thresholds with resolved plan and feature names.
functions.notes: Array of {id (GPLAN_ID), plan, behavior, feature ("all" for FTYPE_ID 0), candidateCap, scoringCap, sendToRedo}, sorted by (GPLAN_ID, canonical behavior position; unknown behaviors last), stable within ties. Requires CFG_GENERIC_THRESHOLD, CFG_GPLAN and CFG_FTYPE (else MISSING_SECTION).

functions.name: validate_generic_threshold
functions.doc: Stage the checks of a generic-threshold add without mutating the config, returning the outcome as data.

args.name: plan
args.semantics: Uppercased, matched exactly against GPLAN_CODE; unknown = result notFound/plan (data, not an error).

args.name: behavior
args.semantics: Uppercased; checked against the canonical behavior codes only in the last stage.

args.name: send_to_redo
args.semantics: Case-insensitive Yes/No; checked only in the last stage.

args.name: feature
args.semantics: Absent or "all" (any case) = FTYPE_ID 0. Else uppercased exact FTYPE_CODE match; unknown = result notFound/feature.

functions.notes: Result is the versioned object (schema sz-configtool.generic-threshold-check/v1, root-library Serialize for GenericThresholdCheck): {"schema", "result": "ok" | "duplicate" | "notFound" (+ "which": "plan"|"feature", "value": uppercased code) | "invalid" (+ "failures": [{"field", "reasonCode", "offendingValue"}], order [behavior, sendToRedo])}. Stages stop at the first hit: plan, feature, duplicate (plan, behavior, feature), then field validation. Missing sections are NOT errors (a missing CFG_GPLAN is notFound/plan). Caps are not taken.
functions.c_notes: The C export returns the identical payload. C typed export takes every arg (feature NULL = ALL).

functions.name: validate_config
functions.doc: Check that a document has the top-level shape of a config (structure only).
functions.notes: Checks, in order: valid JSON (JSON_PARSE); a G2_CONFIG key (MISSING_SECTION) that is an object (INVALID_STRUCTURE); every recognised CFG_* section (validation::EXPECTED_SECTIONS, 27 names) that is PRESENT is an array (INVALID_STRUCTURE). Absent sections, other keys and cross-references are not checked.
functions.c_notes: C typed export returns the text "OK" on success.

functions.name: get_version
functions.doc: Get the configuration VERSION string (G2_CONFIG.CONFIG_BASE_VERSION.VERSION).
functions.notes: Result is a JSON string (e.g. "4.4.0" in the template). Absent or non-string VERSION (or any missing parent) = NOT_FOUND.
functions.c_notes: C typed export returns the bare (unquoted) string and reports library errors with returnCode -5 and no reason code.

functions.name: get_compatibility_version
functions.doc: Get COMPATIBILITY_VERSION.CONFIG_VERSION.
functions.notes: Result is a JSON string (e.g. "11" in the template). Absent or non-string CONFIG_VERSION (or any missing parent) = NOT_FOUND.
functions.c_notes: C typed export returns the bare string and reports library errors with returnCode -5 and no reason code.

functions.name: update_compatibility_version
functions.doc: Set COMPATIBILITY_VERSION.CONFIG_VERSION.

args.name: new_version
args.semantics: Stored verbatim as a JSON string; no format validation.

functions.notes: Absent CONFIG_BASE_VERSION or COMPATIBILITY_VERSION = NOT_FOUND; COMPATIBILITY_VERSION not an object = INVALID_CONFIG. TRAP: an absent G2_CONFIG is NOT an error — the config is returned unchanged (re-serialized).
